additionalCoursework:
Other recommended courses include:
-Diversity: Courses that focus on the culture, history and/or current circumstances of diverse populations
-Ethics: Courses that address questions and issues related to morality and moral behavior that may include meta-ethics, normative ethics, applied ethics, moral psychology and descriptive ethics

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Ohio State’s College of Medicine recognizes that a class with rich and varied lived experiences promotes cultural awareness, understanding, and creates an appreciation for the importance of producing physicians who can better serve a robust community. The MEDPATH program’s aim is to increase the number students from educationally and/or socioeconomically disadvantaged backgrounds who enter medical school, and who show evidence of a commitment to practice in a medically underserved community. Visit https://medicine.osu.edu/education/medpath-program to learn more.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: OSUCOM supports over 160 student organizations in a variety of themes and areas. Visit https://medicine.osu.edu/departments/office-of-student-life/student-organizations for a list of current organizations and interest groups.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Ohio State University has the nation's largest single college campus and the resources that go with it. Columbus offers many opportunities to engage in the arts, cultural events, festivals, restaurants, sports, and nightlife. Learn more by visiting https://careers.wexnermedical.osu.edu/about-us/columbus
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
On campus housing for professional students is available. Visit https://housing.osu.edu/incoming-students/graduate-professional-and-non-traditional-housing/ to learn more.  

Off campus housing is available. The Victorian Village and Grandview Heights neighborhoods are are popular for medical students. Rent ranges depending on a variety of factors ($400-2000 monthly). The university offers support for students who live off campus through the Willie J. Young, Sr. Off-Campus and Commuter Student Engagement Office ( https://offcampus.osu.edu )
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: All Ohio State students have access to support through the Office of Disability Services: https://slds.osu.edu/.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: The College of Medicine has an embedded mental health counselor on staff who offers medical students individual counseling free of charge. The college also contracts with the Wexner Medical Center to offer psychological and psychiatric health care to medical students, also free of charge. A meditation room, gym, and humanities lounge are available specifically for medical students. Financial wellness programs covering topics from student loan repayment plans to homebuying to transitioning to residency are offered throughout the curriculum. Academic wellness programs include 1:1 academic coaching, peer tutoring, faculty tutoring, and take-a-break events during dedicated study for Step 1. The Humanism and the Arts in Medicine program offers a variety of activities for students to engage and develop their compassion and creativity.  You can learn more about many of these offerings by visiting https://medicine.osu.edu/departments/office-of-student-life
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The Ohio State College of Medicine features a dynamic campus life that drives academic excellence through promoting diverse perspectives. Our learners actively collaborate with a supportive network of faculty and peers to enhance the curriculum and optimize the clinical learning environment. This approach cultivates a sense of belonging and fosters a powerful sense of advocacy within our students, making Ohio State an ideal place for aspiring medical professionals to develop and thrive. 

The broader university campus experience offers a plethora of clubs, organizations, sporting ventures, volunteer opportunities and cultural events that enhance student life, promoting well-rounded personal and professional growth.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students will need transportation to clinical sites. Public transportation is available within the city of Columbus, including through COTA, where Ohio State students can ride using their student ID: https://ttm.osu.edu/bus/cota

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Information on appearance requirements is available in the student handbook: https://medicine.osu.edu/student-resources/student-handbook/professionalism
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Academic support services are available through the Office of Student Life: https://medicine.osu.edu/departments/office-of-student-life/learning-support
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Beginning in week 9 of the first year, students are assigned to a practice  in which they interview and examine patients and perform basic office procedures like EKGs, injections, blood draws, etc.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lectures, electronic modules for independent learning, discussion groups, and team-based learning activities are all used in the OSUCOM curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations begin after completing USMLE Step 1 at the end of the 2nd year of the curriculum. All major core clerkship rotations are performed at one of OSUWMC 7 hospitals or affiliates.
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: 6 week Pre-Entry program in gross anatomy, immunology, biochemistry from med school professors. Seats for this optional activity are limited, with candidates invited to apply after acceptance.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are clustered into quartiles; not ranked from 1-200.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Ohio State's Lead.Serve.Inspire (LSI) curriculum has been developed to prepare tomorrow's physicians to deliver the highest quality care to a diverse population of patients.  Presented as a three-part, four year experience, the LSI curriculum fully integrates foundational and clinical science throughout the four-year period.  

Highlights include:
1) Beginning week 9 of the first year, students attend clinic twice a month where they interview and examine patients and perform basic office procedures
2) Each student meets with an individual faculty coach regularly throughout the 4 years
3) Students will obtain advanced certification in specific areas of their interest
4) All students will achieve competency in the 6 core areas required of graduating residents

 The goal of the LSI curriculum is to ensure that all students are prepared to excel in their chosen post-graduate residency programs and from there to move on to their areas of specialization and physician practices. Visit https://medicine.osu.edu/education/md/curriculum to learn more.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The Ohio State University College of Medicine participates in state and federal scholarship programs that encourage students interested in primary care specialties to practice in underserved areas.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Many first year medical students participate in the College of Medicine's funded research experience for the summer between Med 1 and Med 2. The College of Medicine also encourages and offers technical support for those students applying for off-campus, grant-based research, such as Sarnoff Fellowships or research at the NIH.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students are required to complete a Community Health Education project.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Nationwide Children's Hospital, the home of OSU's Dept of Pediatrics is consistently ranked as one of the top children's hospitals in the United States.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Pass/Fail in years 1 and 2. Honors, Letter of Commendation, Satisfactory in years 3 and 4.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Since 1914 The Ohio State University College of Medicine has blended traditional medical education, innovative learning opportunities, and a strong reputation in the preparation of students for primary care and specialized residencies, encouraging research interests and a strong emphasis on a personalized approach to patient care.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The Ohio State University College of Medicine seeks to recruit self-directed learners who are driven to become empathetic physicians providing evidence-based, compassionate medical care.  The Admissions Committee will assemble a class that displays diversity in background and thought, strong intellect, and the potential to improve people's lives through innovation in research, education, patient care and community service.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: In addition to the minimum 2 required letters, an additional, third letter of reference that speaks to the applicant's character, work ethic, collegiality, etc. is highly recommended. More letters are accepted, as well. These letters typically come from research PIs, employers, physician mentors, coaches, or other course instructors, etc.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: One letter must be submitted from a professor who instructed and assigned you a grade for credit in a course that falls into the BCPM subject classification (Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Math).
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The format of the 2026-2027 interview season will be virtual. Informational sessions are in the morning and two individual interviews are held in the afternoon, one with a faculty admission committee member and one with a student, resident, or fellow admission committee member.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: 1 on 1 interview, blinded to academic record (MCAT and grades)
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: The format of the 2026-2027 interview season will be virtual.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants who are AMCAS verified and who broadly meet holistic admissions criteria.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: International applicants who are not Visa holders or permanent residents are not eligible to apply. Refugees or asylees, DACA, and those in Adjustment of Status are eligible to apply.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Yes, eligible after the first 12 months. Once it is established, it does not need to be renewed. Visit https://registrar.osu.edu/student-hub/ohio-residency-for-tuition/ to learn more.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: All out of state applicants considered
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
**Information for 2027 Admissions Cycle**

We understand the stress and uncontrollable factors associated with the past few years. All aspects of preparation for medical school were impacted by the viral pandemic, the calls of action to address racial injustices, the SCOTUS decision impacting the use of race in admissions, and ongoing legal changes and challenges at the national level.  We remain committed to a holistic approach in consideration of all candidates while ensuring legal compliance. It is our aim to remain considerate of these factors while remaining true to our mission. This information may be updated periodically.

Please note the following information regarding interviews, coursework, labs, letters of evaluation, MCAT, essays, and deadlines: 
•	The format of the 2026-2027 interview season will be virtual. Optional in-person tours will be available monthly for those invited to interview.
•	Pass/Fail Coursework – Pass/Fail will be allowed for all coursework taken during the Spring 2020 term, including pre-requisites taken during this time frame only.
•	Online Coursework and Labs – Online labs will be accepted for the Spring 2020 and Summer 2020 term.
•	Letters of Evaluation – The requirement for a letter of recommendation from the instructor of a graded science course has been changed for the Spring 2020 term.  A letter of recommendation from the instructor of a science course taken pass/fail in the Spring 2020 term is acceptable.
•	MCAT - A valid MCAT score is required to receive a secondary at The Ohio State University College of Medicine. For the current application cycle, the MCAT testing date must be between 1/1/2023 and 9/30/2026.
•	Deadlines - The deadline to request a Secondary Application is 11/02/2026.  The deadline to complete the Secondary Application is 12/01/26.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our medical school considers metrics, along with experiences and attributes, as part of a holistic review.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants who meet the unpublished minimum and citizenship requirements by the primary deadline are invited to complete a secondary application. Candidates who qualify for a secondary application are screened, provided they submit their secondary application by the deadline.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Postbacc and graduate GPAs are considered, in combination with undergrad GPAs, to form a complete academic picture.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We will accept coursework from a community college. We suggest the majority of pre-requisite coursework be taken at a four-year institution, when possible.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
Candidates invited for an interview are given the opportunity to submit an update letter prior to their interview date. 

Letters of intent are discouraged and do not have any impact on admission decisions.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Technical standards for medical student admission, retention, and graduation is available on the OSUCOM website. Accepted students are required to complete a Technical Standard Attestation prior to matriculation.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: There are several scholarships and grants available to admitted students. The scholarships are awarded based predominantly on merit using prior academic performance as the standard measure. There are also numerous donor-funded scholarships with special eligibility criteria based on the donor(s)’ directives at the time the scholarships were established. The institution also awards need-based grants utilizing the financial information as reported on the FAFSA. Federal student loan eligibility is awarded to backfill any remaining unmet need to bring the student up to their full Cost of Attendance (COA).

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Primary Care Track (PCT) - The College offers a 3-year program leading to the MD degree for students with a strong desire to practice primary care. More information provided by our website : https://medicine.osu.edu/education/md/curriculum/three-year-primary-care-track 
Email: threeyeartrack@osumc.edu.

Community Medicine Track (CMT) - The College will offers a 4-year program leading to the MD degree for students with a strong desire to practice any specialty in rural and smaller communities. These 15 students will spend the first two years in Columbus and the third and fourth years in Lima, OH at Mercy Health - St. Rita's. More information provided by our website : https://medicine.osu.edu/education/md/community-medicine-track
Email: communitymedicinetrack@osumc.edu.
MD-PhD, MD-JD, MD-MPH, MD-MHA, and MD-MBA programs are all available.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Interview Season - late August through March
First day acceptance notifications can be issued
“Plan to Enroll” option becomes available for accepted students in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tool.
Accepted applicants may hold no more than three acceptances (if applicable).

“Commit to Enroll” required for MSTP applicants.  Commitment must be made by 5:00 pm on this date. At this time you must withdraw from all waitlists on which you remain and from any other acceptances you are holding ( if applicable) to indicate your final decision to matriculate.
"Commit to Enroll" becomes available for accepted applicants in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School Tool. You are encouraged to indicate your status as soon as possible.

“Commit to Enroll” for Three Year Primary Care Track applicants. Commitment must be made by 5:00 pm on this date. At this time you must withdraw from all waitlists on which you remain and from any other acceptances you are holding ( if applicable) to indicate your final decision to matriculate at our school.

“Commit to Enroll” required of applicants accepted to the Regular MD and CMT program prior to the start Orientation Monday, August 10, 2026. Commitment must be made by 5:00 pm on this date. Non-compliance with these deadlines, especially for Commit to Enroll, may lead to the forfeiture of your seat in the incoming class.

Withdrawal Process – Accepted students are expected to notify us via email anytime during the application process of their decision to matriculate in another medical school by email at medicine@osu.edu.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The Primary Care Track (PCT) is designed for students pursuing family medicine and offers an accelerated three-year MD pathway with a directed route into the OSU Family and Community Medicine Residency. If you meet OSU COM graduation standards and choose to rank us, you will be positioned to match into the OSU FCM Residency through the National Resident Matching Program.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicant must have a strong motivation to enter a career in family medicine and a record predictive of success in an accelerated three-year program.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Application process and requirements are available at listed at https://medicine.osu.edu/education/md/three-year-primary-care-track.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Students must meet all requirements of OSU’s College of Medicine for the MD program to be considered for admission into the Primary Care Track. In addition, students must have the necessary competencies to be successful in an accelerated three-year program.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option available to Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Waitlisted students are evaluated on their overall score, which combines the experiences, attributes, academic metrics, and interview performance.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Biology - one year
General chemistry - one year including lab work
Organic chemistry - one year including lab work
Physics - one year including lab work 
Biochemistry - one semester or quarter

All required premedical coursework must be completed by the established Commit to Enroll deadline.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Completed applications are subjected to a holistic review process to ensure that all eligible candidates are considered. Following the philosophy of AAMC Holistic Review, candidates for admission to the Ohio State University College of Medicine are evaluated based on a balanced consideration of their experiences, attributes, and academic metrics.  Factors considered include clinical experiences, community service, leadership activities, research experience, recommendations, suitability for the study of medicine, and extracurricular activities.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: The admissions committee places value on several types of healthcare-related experiences. Examples included physician shadowing, but include volunteer or employed work in a health care setting, nursing home, free clinic, etc.
